chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'at ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Indeed, Allah Mighty and Majestic has made His friend a target for His enemy in this world.'

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: this world — the transient worldly life as the arena of trial and opposition
key_terms.جَعَلَ: has made/decreed — indicating a deliberate divine act of arrangement and ordainment
key_terms.عَدُوِّهِ: His enemy — the enemy of Allah, referring to those who oppose the awliya of Allah
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for Allah denoting His absolute power and sublimity
key_terms.غَرَضاً: a target or mark — one set up to receive the strikes and opposition of the enemy
key_terms.وَلِيَّهُ: His friend/ally — the one who is close to Allah, encompassing the Imam and the sincere believer

ai.seo_question: Why do the awliya of Allah face such intense opposition and trials in this world?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), conveys that Allah Mighty and Majestic has decreed that His wali (friend/ally) in this world is placed as a target before His enemy. The statement affirms that the trials and enmity directed at the believer — and particularly at the Imams (peace be upon them) — are not accidental but are part of a divinely ordained arrangement. It contextualizes worldly affliction within the framework of Allah's will, calling the believer to patience and steadfast acceptance.
